claim: Let \(N=4k+2\ge6\), and let \(G_N\) be the \(N/2\)-cross-polytope (cocktail-party) graph, that is, \(K_N\) with a perfect matching removed. Under the uniform adjacency Hamiltonian, for a removed matched pair \((u,\bar u)\), define \(P_N(t)=|\langle\bar u|e^{-itA(G_N)}|u\rangle|^2\). Then \[\max_{t\in\mathbb R}P_N(t)=\cos^2(\pi/N),\]with equality at \(t=\pi/2\pm\pi/N\pmod{\pi}\). In particular, the value emphasized by Tsomokos, Plenio, de Vega, and Huelga at \(t=\pi/2\), namely \(P_N(\pi/2)=(1-2/N)^2\), is not the global optimum. The exact optimal infidelity is \(\sin^2(\pi/N)\sim\pi^2/N^2\), whereas the source-time infidelity is \(4/N-4/N^2\), so optimizing the transfer time improves the asymptotic error from order \(N^{-1}\) to order \(N^{-2}\). The proof uses the exact amplitude \[A_N(t)=-\frac12+\left(\frac12-\frac1N\right)e^{2it}+\frac1N e^{-i(N-2)t}\]and, writing \(N=2m\) with odd \(m\), the identity \[1-|A_N(t)|^2=\frac{m-1}{m}\cos^2t+\frac1m\cos^2((m-1)t)+\frac{m-1}{m^2}\sin^2(mt),\]followed by a sharp one-variable trigonometric minimization.

correctness.rationale: The exact antipodal amplitude is reconstructed from the cocktail-party adjacency spectrum. The identity for \(1-|A_N(t)|^2\) reduces the global optimization to a sharp trigonometric minimum, and the candidate times attain equality. Direct matrix checks agree.
